clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, a 45-year-old male, initially presented with neurological symptoms of imbalance, diplopia, slurred speech, progressing to inability to walk, dysphagia, and dysarthria over six years, alongside a persistent erythematous plaque on the right scapular region. Skin lesion biopsy revealed histiocytic proliferation with atypical mitosis and eosinophils, and immunohistochemistry confirmed positivity for CD1a, S100, and langerin, diagnostic of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH). Brain MRI initially showed diffuse encephalic volume loss and multiple hyperintense T2/Flair lesions affecting predominantly the cerebellar regions. A subsequent MRI two months later identified an expansive right parietal extra-axial calcified lesion involving meninges and bone, compressing the brain, consistent with histiocytosis bone involvement. Clinical neurological examination findings were not available in the records. Clinical progression and imaging findings together support CNS involvement by LCH explaining the neurological deterioration.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Histopathology of the skin lesion revealed proliferating histiocytic cells with atypical mitosis and eosinophilic infiltration.
Immunohistochemistry of skin biopsy was positive for CD1a, S100, and langerin markers confirming Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
Initial brain MRI showed diffuse encephalic volume loss and multiple hyperintense lesions in T2/Flair mainly impairing cerebellar bridge and peduncles.

Follow-up brain MRI two months later demonstrated an expansive right parietal extra-axial calcified lesion involving meninges and bone, compressing brain, suggesting histiocytosis bone lesion consistent with LCH.

remaining_uncertainties: Neurological examination findings correlating neurological deficits with imaging and diagnosis were not documented.
